chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dissimulation (applicable) regarding drinking Al-Nabeez'.

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A specific type of fermented drink (often date or grape based) in early Islamic jurisprudence, distinct from wine (khamr).
key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Dissimulation or prudence in concealing one's beliefs or actions to avoid harm, a key concept in Shia theology and jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dissimulation regarding the consumption of Al-Nabeez?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that consuming Al-Nabeez (a mild, non-intoxicating date or grape drink) does not require *taqiyyah* (dissimulation), distinguishing it from wine which is strictly forbidden. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the jurisprudential nuance that while Al-Nabeez is permissible, its mild nature means one need not conceal its consumption to avoid confusion with stronger intoxicants, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contextual clarity in dietary laws.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Usman Bin Isa, from Saeed Bin Yasaar who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is no dissimulation (applicable) regarding drinking Al-Nabeez’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sa‘id ibn Yasar who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘There is no Taqiyah (maintaining caution because of fear) in the case of al-Nabidh (wine).”’
